page: Microsoft Azure D2d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration engineered for standard cloud computing tasks requiring balanced resources and fast scratch space. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. The allocation provides two dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical execution core with two hardware threads. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache, with hardware instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic AES.

The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of the general-purpose tier. Unlike diskless Azure variants, the D2d_v4 integrates an 81 GB local SSD designed for temporary storage, swap partitions, and transient cache. The instance does not feature dedicated GPU acceleration, relying strictly on CPU resources for computing requirements.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate solid single-thread performance alongside constrained multi-threaded capacity due to the two-vCPU hardware footprint. In Geekbench testing, the server scores 1173.0 in single-core metrics, representing an average performance tier, while multi-core scoring reaches 1440.0. In stress-ng tests, CPU performance scales from 1404.68 on a single core to 1846.98 across multiple cores. Memory bandwidth drops from 102.96 GB/sec for small 16 KB cached reads to 12.21 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and 8.99 GB/sec for write operations. Web throughput registers at 1.95 GB/sec, while Redis settlement reaches 1.75 million SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2d_v4 serves as an entry-level dual-thread platform that minimizes resource overhead while including attached high-speed solid-state disk space. Its throughput profile makes it appropriate for lightweight enterprise workloads, including web servers, development environments, small microservices, and staging applications that utilize temporary local caching without exhausting compute reserves.
description: Microsoft Azure D2d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. It offers 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyperthreading, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM and 81 GB of local SSD storage. The system does not include a GPU. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance yields average single-core throughput, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 1173.0 and gzip compression speeds of 23.88 GB/sec. However, multi-core capacity is inherently limited by the two-thread ceiling, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1440.0 and Redis throughput of 1.75 million operations per second. With its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration and integrated scratch disk, the D2d_v4 is suited for lightweight web serving, development environments, small background workers, and microservices requiring temporary local caching.
